nodes.name: MediaLogix
descriptions: Ad performance tracking system migrating from SSIS to C#

Hosts 9 documented databases (Merge d757b12 — 2026-06-12 — Alicia Salazar): Megatron, EndeavorCentral, MegatronRepository, OutboundFeeds, PetFinder, Prime, RedDawn, Trax, WEB. Two further databases (DataManager, scheduler) exist on the same server but are not accessible to the audit account. Megatron is the fastest-growing database in the estate at ~6.6 GB / 30 days (~79 GB/yr). See docs/databases/ and docs/etl/usage-analysis/REPORT.md.

The 9 MediaLogix databases (Megatron, EndeavorCentral, MegatronRepository, OutboundFeeds, PetFinder, Prime, RedDawn, Trax, WEB) appear to be reachable via two routes during the active AWS→Azure migration: legacy 20.51.108.231 (per Alicia's schema dumps 2026-06-11) and Azure target 74.179.80.27 (usw2-db-ml-vm-p). Identical row counts across both routes suggest live synchronization.

nodes.name: Server IP discrepancy 2026-06-14
descriptions: docs/databases/<db>.md (for all 9 MediaLogix databases) and dumps/megatron.sql consistently list 20.51.108.231:1433 as the host for Megatron, RedDawn, Prime, EndeavorCentral, MegatronRepository, OutboundFeeds, PetFinder, Trax, and WEB. Independent connection testing in docs/etl/usage-analysis/REPORT.md connects to those databases via 74.179.80.27:1433 (returning @@SERVERNAME = usw2-db-ml-vm-p), while 20.51.108.231:1433 separately returns @@SERVERNAME = CIM-PROD-SQL01 with the Central Inventory database (no Megatron present). Awaits human resolution: either the per-DB docs have a copy-paste error in the Reach line, or there are two routes to the same backend that differ in observable @@SERVERNAME. Surfaced by Merge d757b12 — 2026-06-12 — Alicia Salazar.

RESOLUTION HYPOTHESIS (added 2026-06-14, derived from wiki + KG synthesis only): the discrepancy is most likely explained by the active AWS→Azure migration that the wiki already documents: Confluence-Findings.md line 15 ('two primary SQL servers on AWS (migrating to Azure)') and line 233 ('Cloud: AWS (primary today), Azure (target — active migration underway)'); the KG node MediaLogix is described as 'Ad performance tracking system migrating from SSIS to C#'; and the Azure-region hostname pattern usw2-db-ml-vm-p (US West 2) matches a fresh Azure deployment. Under this hypothesis the 9 MediaLogix databases currently exist on BOTH servers — legacy 20.51.108.231 (CIM-PROD-SQL01, where Alicia's mssql-scripter ran) and Azure target 74.179.80.27 (usw2-db-ml-vm-p, where the audit account ConflictAI has access). Independent row-count verification supports this: Megatron.Account = 2,082,770 on both, Megatron.Listing = 7,429,072 on both, Megatron.ActivityLog ≈ 4.7 M on both — consistent with active synchronization (transactional replication / AG / ADF migration). What CANNOT be confirmed from wiki+KG alone: the synchronization mechanism, the cutover timeline, and whether ConflictAI's grant could ever reach Megatron via the legacy 20.51.108.231 route. Action item: confirm with Ron Mulder (database owner per docs/databases/README.md).

Surfaced 2026-06-14 by the docs/etl/usage-analysis/REPORT.md connection testing; did not appear in any prior wiki / KG / Confluence artifact, consistent with the wiki's documented 'AWS (primary today), Azure (target — active migration underway)' (Confluence-Findings.md line 233).

descriptions: Legacy CIM production SQL Server reachable at 20.51.108.231:1433 (SQL Server 2022 CU9). Hosts Central Inventory (vehicles_removed = 40 M rows / 411 GB), ClientInventory, DataOne, Feedhub. The per-database docs Alicia generated 2026-06-11 also reference 20.51.108.231:1433 as the source for the 9 MediaLogix databases, suggesting either (a) the MediaLogix databases co-existed on this host as the legacy source-of-truth before the Azure migration, or (b) Alicia's mssql-scripter used a network route or named instance that reaches the MediaLogix Azure VM via this IP. Resolution pending owner confirmation (Ron Mulder).
